# Triage of open issues — session @enzzo19 + @benjaminvillagran

> **Request from coach @gviollaz:** review the 20 open technical issues from the audits and decide, issue by issue, **which to take this week, which this month, and which to leave for post-world cup**. You don't have to implement everything — triage is the task.
>
> **Estimated time for the session:** 60-90 min between the two.
>
> **Suggested deadline:** 1 week from today (2026-05-17).
>
> **Expected outcome:** this doc completed with your decisions + comments on each issue closing or tagging.

---

## 0. How to use this doc

For each issue marked below, decide **one option only**:

| Decision | Meaning | Immediate action |
|---|---|---|
| 🟢 **Take** | It will be done in the indicated window (this week / this month). | Comment on the issue: "taken by X, deadline Y". |
| 🟡 **Postpone** | The topic remains valid but goes to post-world cup. | Tag with `priority/low`. |
| 🔴 **Discard** | False positive or the team confirms it was intentional. | Close the issue with an explanation of 1-2 lines. |
| ❓ **Investigate** | More info needed (git blame, bench test) before deciding. | Comment who investigates and deadline. |

**Golden rule of the session:** if you hesitate more than 5 min on an issue, mark 🟡 Postpone and move on. Better to decide 28 issues in 90 min than to waste the session on 3.

## 7. Session rules

1. **Do not start implementing while triaging.** Triage is triage, implementation is later.
2. **If in doubt > 5 min → 🟡 Postpone.** You can pick it up in the next session.
3. **🔴 Discard requires a reason in one line** in the issue comment. Example: "intentional, as decided by Laureano because the robot ALWAYS enters from the left in the rescue zone".
4. **🟢 Take requires assigning someone.** Without an owner, it is not Taken — it is Postponed.
5. **The coach (Gustavo) does NOT decide here.** You two choose, and send him the summary from §5 at the end.
